findings.trigger_anchor: CHANGELOG.md hunk: "unless a throttle marker is present: Bedrock's \"Too many tokens, please wait before trying again\" is a rate limit, retried then walked — one is_throttle_message() rule in routing/ceiling.py serves the adapter and the probe (r251-3)"
findings.cross_file_justification: The diff changes only documentation, but the CHANGELOG, migration doc and SDD hunks all document new runtime behaviour in loa_cheval/routing/ceiling.py (is_throttle_message) and the claude-headless adapter: a free-text marker found in the CLI diagnostic now overrides the PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT classification. The implementing code is outside the diff and could not be read in this session, so this is anchored on the documented contract.
findings.description: The headless adapter's context-limit verdict ("not walked, no breaker count", the rule that prevents an oversized payload from being re-sent to every fallback voice) is now overridden whenever a throttle phrase is present in the CLI diagnostic. The CHANGELOG also states that classification runs on the full diagnostic. A substring match over free text is a weaker signal than a structured error code: any diagnostic that happens to contain the phrase (a provider message embedded in a larger error, or prompt/tool content echoed into the CLI's output) would reclassify a genuine size rejection as a throttle. That path then retries and walks the identical payload to the next configured voice.
findings.failure_mode: A request correctly rejected by the CLI pre-flight for size is reclassified as a rate limit, retried, charged to the breaker, and forwarded unchanged to the next voice in the chain (possibly a different provider or the HTTP route). This defeats the not-walked safeguard and incurs the upload and spend it was designed to avoid; with attacker-shaped prompt content it is a cheap way to force fan-out of one oversized payload across every configured provider.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify throttles from the CLI's structured result (exit code, JSON error type such as Bedrock ThrottlingException, or an explicit HTTP 429) instead of a substring over the full diagnostic. If text matching must remain, restrict it to the CLI's own error line, require the context-limit signature to be absent before reclassifying, and add a test where the throttle phrase appears inside prompt-derived text and the verdict must stay PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT.
